title: Optimal Loss Allocation in a Mean-Field Model of Systemic Risk
abstract: arXiv:2608.18113v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study a systemic-risk control problem in which a central planner allocates losses generated by bank defaults across the surviving institutions. Banks are modeled through their distances to default, evolving as absorbed Brownian motions with downward jumps induced by redistributed default losses. Unlike bailout models, the planner cannot inject external capital or reduce the aggregate loss, and the only admissible intervention is to decide how each endogenous loss is assigned among solvent banks. The objective is to maximize terminal system health, including survival mass as a leading special case and, more generally, increasing concave welfare functionals of the terminal distribution.   Our main result identifies an optimal allocation rule with a simple economic interpretation: losses should be concentrated on the currently healthiest institutions. In discrete time, this rule takes the form of a cutoff or taxing-the-richest policy,

translated_title: 系统风险均值场模型中的最优损失分配
translated_abstract: 我们研究了一个系统风险控制问题，其中中央规划者在幸存机构之间分配由银行违约产生的损失。银行通过其违约距离建模，该距离演化为吸收布朗运动，并带有由重新分配的违约损失引起的向下跳跃。与救助模型不同，规划者不能注入外部资本或减少总损失，唯一允许的干预是决定每个内生损失如何在有偿付能力的银行之间分配。目标是最大化终端系统健康，包括作为主要特殊情况的生存质量，以及更一般地，终端分布的递增凹福利泛函。我们的主要结果确定了一个具有简单经济解释的最优分配规则：损失应集中在当前最健康的机构上。在离散时间中，该规则采取截断或对最富者征税的政策形式。
tldr: 本文提出在系统风险中，最优损失分配策略是将损失集中于最健康的银行，而非救助或分散，以最大化系统终端健康。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes that in systemic risk, the optimal loss allocation strategy concentrates losses on the healthiest banks, rather than bailouts or spreading, to maximize terminal system health.
